etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English enrollen, from Old French enroller.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To enter (a name, etc.) in a register, roll or list

quote.citation: 1855–1858, William H[ickling] Prescott, History of the Reign of Philip the Second, King of Spain, volume (please specify |volume=I to III), Boston, Mass.: Phillips, Sampson, and Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: All the citizens capable of bearing arms enrolled themselves.

quote.citation: 1649, J[ohn] Milton, ΕΙΚΟΝΟΚΛΆΣΤΗΣ [Eikonoklástēs] […], London:  […]  Matthew Simmons, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: An unwritten law of common right, so engraven in the hearts of our ancestors, and by them so constantly enjoyed and claimed, as that it needed not enrolling.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To enlist (someone) or make (someone) a member of
(intransitive) To enlist oneself (in something) or become a member (of something)
